I am submitting zero weight edits to /work/edited: the submitted weights are identical to the starting (Qwen3.5-0.8B with the earlier edit) weights. What I did and what the evidence shows:

- Diagnosis from /practice/baseline: 39.1% baseline accuracy; 52.3% of generations hit the 8192-token cap (0% of those correct); finished answers are 82.0% correct. Failure = degenerate self-doubt re-checking loops ("But…", "No,…") — 27.6% repeated-line fraction in cut-off answers vs 9.6% in finished ones; many truncated answers contain an unterminated \boxed{.
- Teacher-forced measurement (fwd_2: tails of 6 truncated generations + 3 finished ones, hidden states all 25 layers, MLP activations all 24 layers): a clear "loop direction" d separates cut-off from finished texts in every layer and is written ~100× more by layer 23's full-attention output than by any MLP (±10-25 vs <0.2). However, d is load-bearing: orthogonalizing all MLP down_proj writers against d cost −26.95pp (78% cut rate).
- Layer-23 self-attention writes an enormous state-dependent polarity into the residual (an order of magnitude above every other layer). The top readout alignments of that write: digits (−), GSM-style story/time words, and "But/Wait/Let/</think>" announce tokens — none of these polarity directions can be removed or scaled without damaging the model (E_A d-removal in layer-23 o_proj: −1.17pp ± 2.57; Vt2 removal: −3.52pp ± 2.94; junk-direction Vt3 removal on top of a mild edit: −6.25pp ± 2.6; rank-one conclude-boost and Arditi amplification of the </think> readout: catastrophic "</think>" spam, −45.7pp and −21.5pp).
- Conclusion moments ("I'll go with…", "So the answer should be…") are not linearly separable from ordinary positions in MLP-activation space (holdout AUC ≈ 0.7-0.84), so a ROME-style targeted fix for "never completes" was not available; mean-subtracting the write's constant component (aligned with '?', '$', '.') looked mildly good on select (+1.17pp) but clearly negative on confirm_1, so it was rejected and reverted.
- Reducing linear-attention decay (dt_bias −1.5 everywhere), intended to lengthen working memory and cut re-derivation loops: −27.7pp (66% cut). Reverted.

What remains saved in /work: notes.md (full edit log and analysis), /practice untouched, /work/edited = {} (submission).

Why I expect this to score zero rather than negative: the edited weights ARE the starting weights; the score equals original minus original = 0. I chose this because all nine measured edits have measured effects at or below zero, several severely negative.

Honest summary: the loop failure mechanism is real but distributed and entangled with essential computations (massively active final attention layer; the MLP/residual pathway is intolerant to even small removals; the </think> readout is globally too weak but floods instantly when boosted). I could not find a safe, causal repair within the time and forward-pass budget, and I chose not to submit a harmful edit disguised as a repair.
